definition: A fact finder, also known as trier of fact, is an impartial person or examiner designated to appraise the facts underlying a particular matter of a case. For Example:  In a jury trial: the jury is the fact finder that decides what really happened in the case at hand.  In a bench trial: the judge is the fact finder that decides what really happened.  In an official investigation: an agent or committee may be appointed to determine the facts.
